analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/hardware-support.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a documentation block at head lines 248-254 that defines systemAvailable (SystemMemory.availableBytes) under the default `reclaimable` policy, with a `free-only` alternative. No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or prefix-cache storage behavior changes in this diff. I checked it against the supplied threat model (A-001, A-003, A-016, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, T-041 and related entries). The new text covers only provider-local memory admission, and the edited section names no coordinator-visible capacity wire field or platform contract change. It does not touch the SSD prefix-cache controls in T-041 (HMAC names, TTL, KEK, scoping, or the kill switch). It does not affect attestation or authorization. Remaining unverified contract: the documented formula (free+inactive versus the page-cache-inclusive measure with external and purgeable pages) is described but its implementation in SystemMemory.swift was not supplied, so this pass cannot confirm the doc matches the code. If the code counted reclaimable page cache as available, that could only make load admission more permissive, an availability/resource-pressure matter and not a confidentiality regression. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a security regression or a gap requiring a threat-model update. The context around lines 325-346 and 403-406 was reviewed and is not altered by this diff.
